backlog.spec: Replace the SVR with kernel ridge regression / GP-style regression in dual form on the same precomputed combined kernel. Concretely, solve alpha = solve(K_train + lam*I, y_centered) with lam tuned over {0.01, 0.03, 0.1, 0.3, 1.0} by an inner 5-fold KFold(shuffle=True, random_state=seed) scored on Spearman of out-of-fold predictions, then predict K_test @ alpha. Use sklearn.kernel_ridge.KernelRidge(kernel='precomputed', alpha=lam) for clarity. Keep the kernel construction and the rank target transform exactly as they are. This tests whether the epsilon-insensitive loss of SVR is costing accuracy relative to a smooth squared-error fit.
backlog.title: Gaussian process regression instead of SVR on the same kernel

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, compute the Tanimoto kernel Kt and the descriptor RBF kernel Kd separately for train/train and test/train. Then run an inner 5-fold KFold(shuffle=True, random_state=seed) over a small grid: mixing weight w in {0.3, 0.5, 0.7} for K = w*Kt + (1-w)*Kd, and C in {1.0, 5.0, 20.0}, epsilon fixed at 0.05. Because the kernels are precomputed, each inner fit only slices K[np.ix_(tr,tr)] and K[np.ix_(va,tr)], so the whole grid is cheap. Score each config by the Spearman correlation of pooled out-of-fold predictions against the transformed target, pick the best, refit on all training data, and predict the test set with that configuration.
backlog.title: Inner-CV selection of SVR C and kernel mixing weight

backlog.spec: Wrap the existing pipeline in a bagging loop: build the combined K_train and K_test once, then fit 15 SVR models, each on a bootstrap resample (or a random 80% subsample) of the training rows drawn with np.random.default_rng(seed + i), slicing the precomputed kernel accordingly. Average the test predictions across the 15 models after converting each to ranks. Because the kernel is computed once and each fit is on a smaller matrix, the extra cost is modest. This should reduce variance from the SVR support-vector selection, which matters because the final loss is a correlation over a few hundred test molecules.
backlog.title: Seed-bagged ensemble of subsampled SVR fits

backlog.spec: The harness splits folds by Murcko scaffold, so a random inner KFold is optimistic and may select hyperparameters that do not transfer. Add an inner validation that groups training molecules by their Murcko scaffold (rdkit.Chem.Scaffolds.MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles, falling back to the SMILES itself on failure) and uses sklearn.model_selection.GroupKFold(n_splits=5) over those groups to choose SVR C from {1.0, 5.0, 20.0} and the kernel mixing weight from {0.3, 0.5, 0.7}, scoring by Spearman of pooled out-of-fold predictions. Refit on all training data with the winning pair and predict the test set. Keep the featurization and rank target unchanged.
backlog.title: Scaffold-aware inner validation for hyperparameter choice

backlog.spec: Add a local correction on top of the existing kernel SVR in train.py. First fit the current model exactly as it is now and get test predictions. Then compute leave-one-out-style training residuals cheaply: fit the same SVR under 5-fold KFold(shuffle=True, random_state=seed) on the training kernel (slicing with np.ix_) to obtain out-of-fold predictions, and set r_i = y_transformed_i - oof_pred_i. For each test molecule, find its k = 10 most similar training molecules by the combined kernel row K_test (already computed), form weights w = max(K_test_values - 0, 0) ** 2 normalized to sum to one over those k, and compute a weighted mean residual r_hat. Return svr_prediction + 0.3 * r_hat. The idea is that the global kernel model is smooth and systematically misses locally, so a shrunken nearest-neighbour residual term can recover some rank information. Keep the shrinkage at 0.3 and k at 10; do not tune anything else.
backlog.title: Similarity-weighted kNN residual correction

backlog.spec: The Morgan fingerprint in train.py uses RDKit's default atom invariants, which encode element, degree, charge, isotope, attached hydrogens and ring membership, so two metabolically similar fragments that differ in one of those slots hash to different bits and the Tanimoto kernel misses the resemblance. Add a second, coarser Morgan kernel: build radius-2 2048-bit fingerprints with rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator using atomInvariantsGenerator=rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganAtomInvGen(includeRingMembership=False) (if that argument combination is unavailable, pass explicit per-atom invariants that encode only atomic number and heavy-atom degree), form its Tanimoto kernel, and average it with the existing default-invariant Tanimoto kernel and the descriptor RBF kernel with weights 0.25 / 0.25 / 0.5, so the structural half of the mix is split between the fine and coarse views. Keep the target transform and SVR settings unchanged.
backlog.title: Reduced-invariant Morgan kernel added to the mix

backlog.spec: Replace the binary Morgan fingerprint in featurize() with count fingerprints (GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy, radius 2, 2048 bits). Replace tanimoto() with the generalized MinMax kernel for count vectors: K(a,b) = sum(min(a,b)) / sum(max(a,b)). Compute it with scipy.spatial.distance.cdist(A, B, 'cityblock'), using sum(min) = 0.5*(l1_a + l1_b - L1dist) and sum(max) = l1_a + l1_b - sum(min); guard the denominator with np.maximum(..., 1e-9). Keep everything else unchanged: the descriptor RBF kernel, the 0.5/0.5 kernel average, the rank target transform, and SVR(C=5.0, epsilon=0.05).
backlog.title: Count Morgan fingerprints with MinMax kernel

backlog.spec: train.py calls Chem.MolFromSmiles on the raw SMILES in both featurize and descriptors, so salts, counter-ions and solvent fragments contribute bits and distort whole-molecule descriptors such as MolWt, TPSA and the Crippen terms, which then corrupt the descriptor RBF kernel. Add one shared helper, e.g. def to_mol(s), that parses the SMILES, splits it with Chem.GetMolFrags(mol, asMols=True, sanitizeFrags=True), keeps the fragment with the most heavy atoms (ties broken by larger molecular weight), and returns that fragment; fall back to the parsed molecule if fragmenting fails and to None-safe behaviour if parsing fails (in which case substitute a single-carbon molecule so array shapes stay right). Use this helper in both featurize and descriptors so the fingerprint and the descriptors describe the same stripped parent structure. Everything else, including the kernel mix and SVR settings, stays unchanged.
backlog.title: Largest-fragment, salt-stripped canonicalization before featurization

backlog.spec: The descriptor RBF kernel in train.py uses all ~210 RDKit 2D descriptors after a std>0 filter, but many are near-duplicates (several Chi and Kappa connectivity indices, MolWt vs HeavyAtomMolWt vs ExactMolWt, the whole EState family), so the Euclidean distance that drives the RBF kernel is dominated by whichever property happens to be represented most often. After the existing std filter and before standardizing, compute the absolute Pearson correlation matrix of the training descriptor columns with np.corrcoef (nan_to_num it), then greedily walk columns in their original order and drop any column whose absolute correlation with an already-kept column exceeds 0.95. Apply the same kept-column mask to the test descriptors, then continue with the existing z-score-and-clip step and set gamma = 1/n_kept so the bandwidth tracks the reduced dimension. Fingerprints, the kernel mix and the SVR settings stay exactly as they are.
backlog.title: Prune redundant descriptors by pairwise correlation

backlog.spec: Before building the descriptor RBF kernel, reduce the descriptor block to the most informative columns: on the training fold only, compute the absolute Spearman correlation between each standardized descriptor column and the rank-transformed target, and keep the top K columns with K chosen from {20, 50, 100, all} by an inner 5-fold KFold(shuffle=True, random_state=seed) scored by Spearman of out-of-fold predictions. Apply the same column mask to the test descriptors, recompute gamma as 1/K_kept, and otherwise leave the Tanimoto kernel, the 0.5/0.5 mix, the rank target, and the SVR unchanged. Make sure the selection uses only training-fold data so there is no leakage.
backlog.title: Feature-selected descriptor subset by rank correlation

memo: Helped: changing model family (LightGBM 0.5726, Tanimoto-kernel SVR 0.5491, from 0.6103 start), rank-normalizing the target (0.5310/0.5307, replicated), and above all averaging the Tanimoto kernel with an RDKit 2D descriptor RBF kernel (0.4830, incumbent). Did not help: FCFP (0.5877), MACCS (0.5421), stacking (0.5558), MLP ensemble (0.5500), descriptor-only ridge (0.5328), 60-descriptor subset (0.4973), autocorrelation descriptors (0.5057), RankSVM (0.5957), Laplacian solve (0.5716). Within noise (sd about 0.0070): scaffold weighting 0.4803, KernelRidge 0.4822, descriptor weighting 0.4824, extra kernels (0.4854-0.4860). Gobbi kernel (0.4680/0.4791) and ridge prior (0.4711/0.4728) were borderline gains that did not hold up on replication. Kernels look plateaued near 0.48. Next: tune SVR C, epsilon and descriptor gamma; try a GP; try quantile-transformed descriptors; maybe combine Gobbi with the ridge prior. Read train.py first, since many edits aborted by assuming a random forest or LightGBM. Replicate gains under 0.01.
